page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.u1-c1m8.8xlarge is a high-memory compute instance powered by Intel Xeon processors running at a base clock of 2.5 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. Virtualized via KVM, the configuration delivers 32 dedicated vCPUs spanning 16 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading. It is equipped with 256 GB of system memory, providing a high ratio of 8 GB RAM per vCPU. The instance includes hardware vector support through AVX and AVX-512 extensions. Local disk storage is not bundled, requiring external network block storage for persistent data, while baseline network throughput is rated at 10 Gbps.

Empirical benchmark results reflect a system optimized for parallel execution rather than single-threaded speed. In stress-ng and Geekbench evaluations, single-core scores fall into the lower quartile, consistent with its 2.5 GHz base frequency and conservative single-core limits. Conversely, multi-threaded metrics such as Geekbench multi-core and PassMark CPU scores perform within the median cloud average. Memory bandwidth benchmarks demonstrate stable uncached read speeds of 75.14 GB/s and write speeds of 47.31 GB/s. Application tests confirm steady execution across database operations, generating 23.41 million Redis SET operations per second and 17.4 GB/s in static web serving throughput.

The key operational tradeoff centers on per-core speed versus memory density. For applications requiring rapid per-thread execution or low-latency compilation cycles, the modest single-core profile presents a constraint. However, the high memory-to-vCPU allocation yields strong qualitative cost efficiency for systems bound by addressable memory rather than raw compute frequency. The ecs.u1-c1m8.8xlarge is particularly appropriate for distributed caching layers, in-memory databases such as Redis, enterprise backends, and multi-threaded data transformation pipelines.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.u1-c1m8.8xlarge is a memory-oriented virtual machine featuring 32 dedicated vCPUs across 16 physical Intel Xeon cores at 2.5 GHz and 256 GB of system RAM. Built on the x86_64 architecture with KVM virtualization, it provides an 8 GB per vCPU ratio, making it suitable for memory-heavy deployments. The instance does not include bundled local storage, requiring network-attached block devices, and maintains a 10 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. Benchmark evaluations place multi-threaded CPU throughput, compilation tasks, and database processing firmly within the median tier, while single-core performance ranks lower due to conservative clock speeds. Memory throughput remains balanced, achieving over 23 million Redis SET operations per second and steady static web throughput. By trading ultra-high single-thread speed for memory capacity and thread density, the instance delivers resource efficiency for large caching clusters, in-memory databases, memory-bound enterprise applications, and multi-threaded background workers.
